builder_plan.scenario: Profiling shows attention computation is a bottleneck in your self-hosted service.
builder_plan.change: Check the supported GPU, tensor shapes, and precision, then replace only the relevant kernel.
builder_plan.baseline: The existing kernel inside the same complete serving pipeline.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: TauLang: A Language and Compiler for Space-Time Programming on Statically Scheduled Accelerators
summary: TauLang replaces implicit, hardware-resolved scheduling in conventional kernel languages with explicit parameterized time annotations, validated algebraically and solved jointly with tensor placement via an integer linear program. The cost is a new language and compiler toolchain plus ILP solve time, and it presupposes a statically scheduled accelerator such as a Groq TSP rather than a GPU. It fails to apply when the target hardware has dynamic scheduling (caches, arbiters, hardware schedulers), and schedule validity depends on compiler correctness since mistimed operations are correctness errors, not performance regressions.
rationale: The technique targets statically scheduled accelerators like Groq's TSP, which the reader does not possess, so it offers no actionable path on a 24 GB GPU or API-based workflow.
technique: Explicit-time kernel language for static accelerators

claims.statement: TauLang replaces implicit, hardware-resolved scheduling in conventional kernel languages with explicit parameterized time annotations, validated algebraically and solved jointly with tensor placement via an integer linear program. The cost is a new language and compiler toolchain plus ILP solve time, and it presupposes a statically scheduled accelerator such as a Groq TSP rather than a GPU. It fails to apply when the target hardware has dynamic scheduling (caches, arbiters, hardware schedulers), and schedule validity depends on compiler correctness since mistimed operations are correctness errors, not performance regressions.

Joint tensor-placement and cycle scheduling achieves a 1.40x latency speedup across ten kernels over a space-first flow, on a cycle-accurate TSP-like model; explicit time pins keep latency within one cycle of untimed schedules while scaling joint search to 1,636 GEMM blocks where untimed search fails at 32.
